tools.name: list_decks
tools.description: The user's Renderball documents, newest first, with editor links. Needs an account (a key). The design open in the person's editor right now comes first, marked open_now.

tools.name: create_deck
tools.description: Start a new presentation from a brief, the brand and your outline. The brand: if you can open the brand's website, read its real colours and fonts there first and declare them — the lead colour is usually the main buttons and the large coloured areas, not the link colour — and always give the websit

tools.name: write_outline
tools.description: Save a new page-by-page outline for a deck (pages written for the old one are dropped). The reply carries PAGE 1'S BRIEF; each submit_page reply carries the next page's.

tools.name: get_brief
tools.description: The writing brief for a deck whose outline is already saved.

tools.name: see_deck
tools.description: The deck's rendered pages as images, page 1 first — look at them for overlapping or clipped text, odd spacing, an element off its page or a picture that does not say its page's claim, then fix that page and submit_page it again. Available once the deck has been rendered.

tools.name: submit_deck
tools.description: Replace the whole file of a deck whose pages are all written (while pages are still being written, submit_page each one — a whole file is refused then). Renderball checks it against the brief, renders every page and opens it in the editor. Returns 'ready' with the editor_url, or 'importing' — then p

tools.name: deck_status
tools.description: Whether a submitted deck is still importing, ready (with the editor link and the rendered pages, to check them), or failed (with the reason).

tools.name: share_deck
tools.description: Turn on the public link for a deck and return it: anyone with the link can view the deck.

tools.name: get_page_brief
tools.description: The full writing brief for ONE page: the studio's method, the rules, the examples chosen for that page, and (after page 1) page 1's file to continue. You rarely need it: page 1's brief comes with create_deck and each submit_page reply carries the next page's. Use it for a helper that writes one page

tools.name: get_examples
tools.description: Up to 4 of the studio's example pages, by the ids listed in a page brief — read the ones that fit the page you are about to write.

tools.name: submit_page
tools.description: Save one page you wrote (page 1: the file with Section0 and the shared design; page N: only its Section), with its direction (one sentence: the thing, the motion that acts out the claim, one craft detail). A page is accepted only after its brief was handed to you. The reply carries the next page's b

tools.name: read_page
tools.description: Read one page of a design as it is NOW — the code the person's editor shows, including their own edits — before changing it. Use it whenever the person asks to change something in a design that already exists: their editor may hold edits you have not seen. The reply carries the page's code, the code

tools.name: edit_page
tools.description: Change part of a design that already exists, the way you edit a file: each edit replaces exact text from read_page (it must appear exactly once) with new text. Use it for any change the person asks for in an existing design — a headline, a colour, a picture, moving or removing something — instead of

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "create_deck" stacks urgency/override words (always, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.
